1 --- 2 name: mermaidjs-v11 3 description: Create diagrams and visualizations using Mermaid.js v11 syntax. Use when generating flowcharts, sequence diagrams, class diagrams, state diagrams, ER diagrams, Gantt charts, user journeys, timelines, architecture diagrams, or any of 24+ diagram types. Supports JavaScript API integration, CLI rendering to SVG/PNG/PDF, theming, configuration, and accessibility features. Essential for documentation, technical diagrams, project planning, system architecture, and visual communication. 4 --- 5 6 # Mermaid.js v11 7 8 ## Overview 9 10 Create text-based diagrams using Mermaid.js v11 declarative syntax. Convert code to SVG/PNG/PDF via CLI or render in browsers/markdown files. 11 12 ## Quick Start 13 14 **Basic Diagram Structure:** 15 ``` 16 {diagram-type} 17 {diagram-content} 18 ``` 19 20 **Common Diagram Types:** 21 - `flowchart` - Process flows, decision trees 22 - `sequenceDiagram` - Actor interactions, API flows 23 - `classDiagram` - OOP structures, data models 24 - `stateDiagram` - State machines, workflows 25 - `erDiagram` - Database relationships 26 - `gantt` - Project timelines 27 - `journey` - User experience flows 28 29 See `references/diagram-types.md` for all 24+ types with syntax. 30 31 ## Creating Diagrams 32 33 **Inline Markdown Code Blocks:** 34 ````markdown 35 ```mermaid 36 flowchart TD 37 A[Start] --> B{Decision} 38 B -->|Yes| C[Action] 39 B -->|No| D[End] 40 ``` 41 ```` 42 43 **Configuration via Frontmatter:** 44 ````markdown 45 ```mermaid 46 --- 47 theme: dark 48 --- 49 flowchart LR 50 A --> B 51 ``` 52 ```` 53 54 **Comments:** Use `%% ` prefix for single-line comments. 55 56 ## CLI Usage 57 58 Convert `.mmd` files to images: 59 ```bash 60 # Installation 61 npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli 62 63 # Basic conversion 64 mmdc -i diagram.mmd -o diagram.svg 65 66 # With theme and background 67 mmdc -i input.mmd -o output.png -t dark -b transparent 68 69 # Custom styling 70 mmdc -i diagram.mmd --cssFile style.css -o output.svg 71 ``` 72 73 See `references/cli-usage.md` for Docker, batch processing, and advanced workflows. 74 75 ## JavaScript Integration 76 77 **HTML Embedding:** 78 ```html 79 
    80	  flowchart TD
    81	    A[Client] --> B[Server]
    82
83 84 85 ``` 86 87 See `references/integration.md` for Node.js API and advanced integration patterns. 88 89 ## Configuration & Theming 90 91 **Common Options:** 92 - `theme`: "default", "dark", "forest", "neutral", "base" 93 - `look`: "classic", "handDrawn" 94 - `fontFamily`: Custom font specification 95 - `securityLevel`: "strict", "loose", "antiscript" 96 97 See `references/configuration.md` for complete config options, theming, and customization. 98 99 ## Practical Patterns 100 101 Load `references/examples.md` for: 102 - Architecture diagrams 103 - API documentation flows 104 - Database schemas 105 - Project timelines 106 - State machines 107 - User journey maps 108 109 ## Resources 110 111 - `references/diagram-types.md` - Syntax for all 24+ diagram types 112 - `references/configuration.md` - Config, theming, accessibility 113 - `references/cli-usage.md` - CLI commands and workflows 114 - `references/integration.md` - JavaScript API and embedding 115 - `references/examples.md` - Practical patterns and use cases

1	# US-China Trade War: Tariffs, Trade Volumes, and Supply Chain Shifts (2016–2024)
     2	
     3	## Overview
     4	This collection of datasets tracks the evolution of the US-China trade war from 2016 to 2024, covering tariff rate changes, bilateral trade volumes, supply chain diversification patterns, and key policy milestones.
     5	
     6	## Data Source
     7	
     8	### tariff_rates
     9	Average effective tariff rates by half-year period (2017-H1 to 2024-H1). Fields: `period` (string, format YYYY-HX), `us_tariff_on_china` (percent, range 3.1–25.4), `china_tariff_on_us` (percent, range 8.0–23.1). Rates represent trade-weighted averages across all tariff lines.
    10	
    11	### bilateral_trade
    12	Annual US-China bilateral trade from 2016 to 2024. Fields: `year` (integer), `us_exports_to_china` (billion USD), `us_imports_from_china` (billion USD), `total_bilateral` (billion USD, sum of exports and imports).
    13	
    14	### supply_chain_share
    15	Annual share of total US goods imports by source. Fields: `year` (integer), `china` (percent), `vietnam` (percent), `india` (percent), `rest_of_world` (percent). Values for each year sum to approximately 100%.
    16	
    17	### policy_events
    18	Key policy milestones. Fields: `date` (ISO date string), `period_approx` (corresponding half-year period), `event` (short description), `category` (one of: investigation, tariff, deal, review). Contains 12 events spanning August 2017 to May 2024.
    19	
    20	## Data Notes
    21	- Tariff rates are approximate trade-weighted averages and may differ from statutory rates on specific product categories
    22	- 2024 data is partial (H1 only for tariffs; full-year trade figures are estimates)
    23	- Supply chain shares are rounded and may not sum to exactly 100%
    24	- Rest-of-world is a residual category capturing all non-China, non-Vietnam, non-India imports

1	# Mermaid.js Diagram Types
     2	
     3	Comprehensive syntax reference for all 24+ diagram types in Mermaid.js v11.
     4	
     5	## Core Diagrams
     6	
     7	### Flowchart
     8	Process flows, decision trees, workflows.
     9	
    10	**Syntax:**
    11	```
    12	flowchart {direction}
    13	  {nodeId}[{label}] {arrow} {nodeId}[{label}]
    14	```
    15	
    16	**Directions:** TB/TD (top-bottom), BT, LR (left-right), RL
    17	**Shapes:** `()` round, `[]` rect, `{}` diamond, `{{}}` hexagon, `(())` circle
    18	**Arrows:** `-->` solid, `-.->` dotted, `==>` thick
    19	**Subgraphs:** Group related nodes
    20	
    21	### Sequence Diagram
    22	Actor interactions, API flows, message sequences.
    23	
    24	**Syntax:**
    25	```
    26	sequenceDiagram
    27	  participant A as Actor
    28	  A->>B: Message
    29	  activate B
    30	  B-->>A: Response
    31	  deactivate B
    32	```
    33	
    34	**Arrows:** `->` solid, `->>` arrow, `-->` dotted, `-x` cross, `-)` async
    35	**Features:** Loops, alternatives, parallel, optional, critical regions
    36	
    37	### Class Diagram
    38	OOP structures, inheritance, relationships.
    39	
    40	**Syntax:**
    41	```
    42	classDiagram
    43	  class Animal {
    44	    +String name
    45	    -int age
    46	    +void eat()
    47	  }
    48	  Animal <|-- Dog : inherits
    49	```
    50	
    51	**Visibility:** `+` public, `-` private, `#` protected, `~` package
    52	**Relationships:** `<|--` inheritance, `*--` composition, `o--` aggregation, `-->` association
    53	
    54	### State Diagram
    55	State machines, transitions, workflows.
    56	
    57	**Syntax:**
    58	```
    59	stateDiagram-v2
    60	  [*] --> State1
    61	  State1 --> State2 : transition
    62	  State2 --> [*]
    63	```
    64	
    65	**Features:** Composite states, choice points, forks/joins, concurrency
    66	
    67	### ER Diagram
    68	Database relationships, schemas.
    69	
    70	**Syntax:**
    71	```
    72	erDiagram
    73	  CUSTOMER ||--o{ ORDER : places
    74	  ORDER ||--|{ LINE_ITEM : contains
    75	```
    76	
    77	**Cardinality:** `||` one, `|o` zero-one, `}|` one-many, `}o` zero-many
    78	
    79	## Planning Diagrams
    80	
    81	### Gantt Chart
    82	Project timelines, schedules.
    83	
    84	**Syntax:**
    85	```
    86	gantt
    87	  title Project
    88	  dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD
    89	  section Phase1
    90	    Task1 :done, 2024-01-01, 5d
    91	    Task2 :active, after Task1, 3d
    92	```
    93	
    94	**Status:** `done`, `active`, `crit`, `milestone`
    95	
    96	### User Journey
    97	Experience flows, satisfaction tracking.
    98	
    99	**Syntax:**
   100	```
   101	journey
   102	  title User Journey
   103	  section Shopping
   104	    Browse: 5: Customer
   105	    Add to cart: 3: Customer, System
   106	```
   107	
   108	**Scores:** 1-5 satisfaction levels
   109	
   110	### Kanban
   111	Task boards, workflow stages.
   112	
   113	**Syntax:**
   114	```
   115	kanban
   116	  Todo[Task Board]
   117	    task1[Implement API]
   118	    @{ assigned: "Dev1", priority: "High" }
   119	  InProgress[In Progress]
   120	    task2[Fix bug]
   121	```
   122	
   123	### Quadrant Chart
   124	Prioritization, trend analysis.
   125	
   126	**Syntax:**
   127	```
   128	quadrantChart
   129	  x-axis Low --> High
   130	  y-axis Low --> High
   131	  Item A: [0.3, 0.6]
   132	```
   133	
   134	## Architecture Diagrams
   135	
   136	### C4 Diagram
   137	System architecture, components.
   138	
   139	**Syntax:**
   140	```
   141	C4Context
   142	  Person(user, "User")
   143	  System(app, "Application")
   144	  Rel(user, app, "Uses")
   145	```
   146	
   147	### Architecture Diagram
   148	Cloud infrastructure, services.
   149	
   150	**Syntax:**
   151	```
   152	architecture-beta
   153	  service api(server)[API]
   154	  service db(database)[Database]
   155	  api:R --> L:db
   156	```
   157	
   158	**Icons:** cloud, database, disk, internet, server, or iconify.design icons
   159	
   160	### Block Diagram
   161	Module dependencies, networks.
   162	
   163	**Syntax:**
   164	```
   165	block-beta
   166	  columns 3
   167	  a["Block A"] b["Block B"]
   168	  a --> b
   169	```
   170	
   171	**Shapes:** rounded, stadium, cylinder, diamond, trapezoid, hexagon
   172	
   173	## Data Visualization
   174	
   175	### Pie Chart
   176	Proportions, distributions.
   177	
   178	**Syntax:**
   179	```
   180	pie showData
   181	  "Category A" : 45.5
   182	  "Category B" : 30.0
   183	```
   184	
   185	### XY Chart
   186	Trends, comparisons.
   187	
   188	**Syntax:**
   189	```
   190	xychart-beta
   191	  x-axis [jan, feb, mar]
   192	  y-axis "Sales" 0 --> 100
   193	  line [30, 45, 60]
   194	  bar [25, 40, 55]
   195	```
   196	
   197	### Sankey
   198	Flow visualization, resource allocation.
   199	
   200	**Syntax:**
   201	```
   202	sankey-beta

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
import numpy as np
import json

# Load data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json', 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# Extract data
tariff_data = data['tariff_rates']['data']
bilateral_data = data['bilateral_trade']['data']
supply_data = data['supply_chain_share']['data']
policy_events = data['policy_events']['data']

# Prepare tariff data
tariff_periods = [d['period'] for d in tariff_data]
us_tariffs = [d['us_tariff_on_china'] for d in tariff_data]
china_tariffs = [d['china_tariff_on_us'] for d in tariff_data]

# Convert periods to numeric positions (half-year increments from 2017-H1)
tariff_x = []
for p in tariff_periods:
    year, half = p.split('-')
    year = int(year)
    half = 0 if half == 'H1' else 0.5
    tariff_x.append(year + half)
tariff_x = np.array(tariff_x)

# Prepare bilateral trade data (annual)
trade_years = [d['year'] for d in bilateral_data]
trade_total = [d['total_bilateral'] for d in bilateral_data]
trade_exports = [d['us_exports_to_china'] for d in bilateral_data]
trade_imports = [d['us_imports_from_china'] for d in bilateral_data]
trade_x = np.array(trade_years, dtype=float)

# Prepare supply chain data
supply_years = [d['year'] for d in supply_data]
china_share = [d['china'] for d in supply_data]
vietnam_share = [d['vietnam'] for d in supply_data]
india_share = [d['india'] for d in supply_data]
row_share = [d['rest_of_world'] for d in supply_data]
supply_x = np.array(supply_years, dtype=float)

# Prepare policy events
event_dates = []
event_labels = []
event_periods = []
for e in policy_events:
    date = e['date']
    year = int(date.split('-')[0])
    month = int(date.split('-')[1])
    event_dates.append(year + (month - 1) / 12)
    event_labels.append(e['event'])
    event_periods.append(e['period_approx'])

# Color scheme - editorial, professional
COLOR_US_TARIFF = '#1f4e79'      # Deep blue
COLOR_CHINA_TARIFF = '#c0504d'   # Muted red
COLOR_TRADE_TOTAL = '#4f81bd'    # Medium blue
COLOR_TRADE_FILL = '#dce6f1'     # Light blue fill
COLOR_CHINA_SHARE = '#1f4e79'    # Deep blue
COLOR_VIETNAM_SHARE = '#9cbb58'  # Green
COLOR_INDIA_SHARE = '#f79646'    # Orange
COLOR_ROW_SHARE = '#d9d9d9'      # Light gray

# Setup figure with 3 subplots sharing x-axis
fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 1, figsize=(16, 18), sharex=False, 
                          gridspec_kw={'height_ratios': [1, 1.1, 1.2], 'hspace': 0.08})

# Common x-range
x_min = 2016.5
x_max = 2024.5

# ===================== PANEL 1: TARIFF RATES =====================
ax1 = axes[0]

# Step plot for tariffs
ax1.step(tariff_x, us_tariffs, where='mid', color=COLOR_US_TARIFF, linewidth=2.5, 
         label='US Tariff on Chinese Goods', zorder=3)
ax1.step(tariff_x, china_tariffs, where='mid', color=COLOR_CHINA_TARIFF, linewidth=2.5, 
         linestyle='--', label='China Retaliatory Tariff on US Goods', zorder=3)

# Fill between to emphasize gap
ax1.fill_between(tariff_x, us_tariffs, china_tariffs, step='mid', alpha=0.12, color='gray')

ax1.set_ylabel('Average Effective Tariff Rate (%)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_title('US-China Trade War: Tariff Escalation, Trade Volume Shifts, and Supply Chain Diversion (2016–2024)',
              fontsize=15, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax1.set_xlim(x_min, x_max)
ax1.set_ylim(0, 28)
ax1.legend(loc='upper left', fontsize=10, framealpha=0.9)
ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linestyle='-', linewidth=0.5)
ax1.tick_params(axis='both', labelsize=10)

# Add policy event annotations for tariff-related events on panel 1
tariff_events = [e for e in policy_events if e['category'] in ['tariff', 'investigation']]
for i, e in enumerate(tariff_events):
    date = e['date']
    year = int(date.split('-')[0])
    month = int(date.split('-')[1])
    x_pos = year + (month - 1) / 12
    
    # Alternate annotation placement
    y_offset = 24 if i % 2 == 0 else 20
    va = 'bottom' if i % 2 == 0 else 'top'
    
    ax1.annotate(e['event'], xy=(x_pos, us_tariffs[min(int((x_pos-2017)*2), len(us_tariffs)-1)] if x_pos >= 2017 else 3.1),
                xytext=(x_pos, y_offset),
                fontsize=7.5, ha='center', va=va,
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#555555', lw=0.8, 
                               connectionstyle='arc3,rad=0.1'),
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.2', facecolor='#fffacd', edgecolor='gray', alpha=0.9))

# ===================== PANEL 2: BILATERAL TRADE VOLUME =====================
ax2 = axes[1]

# Line for total bilateral trade
ax2.plot(trade_x, trade_total, color=COLOR_TRADE_TOTAL, linewidth=2.5, marker='o', 
         markersize=6, label='Total Bilateral Trade', zorder=3)
ax2.fill_between(trade_x, trade_total, alpha=0.15, color=COLOR_TRADE_TOTAL)

# Add export/import components as stacked area effect
ax2.plot(trade_x, trade_exports, color='#70ad47', linewidth=1.5, linestyle='--', 
         marker='s', markersize=4, label='US Exports to China', alpha=0.8)
ax2.plot(trade_x, trade_imports, color='#c0504d', linewidth=1.5, linestyle='--', 
         marker='^', markersize=4, label='US Imports from China', alpha=0.8)

# Annotate key points
peak_idx = np.argmax(trade_total)
dip_idx = np.argmin(trade_total)
ax2.annotate(f'Peak: ${trade_total[peak_idx]:.1f}B', 
             xy=(trade_x[peak_idx], trade_total[peak_idx]),
             xytext=(trade_x[peak_idx]-0.8, trade_total[peak_idx]+30),
             fontsize=9, fontweight='bold', color='#1f4e79',
             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#1f4e79', lw=1))
ax2.annotate(f'Dip: ${trade_total[dip_idx]:.1f}B', 
             xy=(trade_x[dip_idx], trade_total[dip_idx]),
             xytext=(trade_x[dip_idx]+0.8, trade_total[dip_idx]-30),
             fontsize=9, fontweight='bold', color='#c0504d',
             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#c0504d', lw=1))

ax2.set_ylabel('Trade Volume (Billion USD)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xlim(2016, 2024.5)
ax2.set_ylim(400, 750)
ax2.legend(loc='upper right', fontsize=10, framealpha=0.9)
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linestyle='-', linewidth=0.5)
ax2.tick_params(axis='both', labelsize=10)

# Add Phase One deal annotation
phase_one_date = 2020.04  # Jan 15, 2020
ax2.axvline(x=phase_one_date, color='#7030a0', linestyle=':', linewidth=2, alpha=0.8)
ax2.annotate('Phase One Deal Signed', xy=(phase_one_date, 650), fontsize=9, 
             color='#7030a0', fontweight='bold', ha='center',
             bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.2', facecolor='#e6e0ec', edgecolor='#7030a0', alpha=0.9))

# ===================== PANEL 3: SUPPLY CHAIN SHARES =====================
ax3 = axes[2]

# Stacked area chart
ax3.stackplot(supply_x, china_share, vietnam_share, india_share, row_share,
              labels=['China', 'Vietnam', 'India', 'Rest of World'],
              colors=[COLOR_CHINA_SHARE, COLOR_VIETNAM_SHARE, COLOR_INDIA_SHARE, COLOR_ROW_SHARE],
              alpha=0.85, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5)

# Add trend lines for emphasis on the key story
ax3.plot(supply_x, china_share, color='white', linewidth=2, linestyle='-', alpha=0.7)
ax3.plot(supply_x, vietnam_share, color='white', linewidth=2, linestyle='-', alpha=0.7)
ax3.plot(supply_x, india_share, color='white', linewidth=2, linestyle='-', alpha=0.7)

# Highlight the divergence with annotations
ax3.annotate(f'China: {china_share[0]:.1f}% → {china_share[-1]:.1f}%', 
             xy=(supply_x[0], china_share[0]/2), xytext=(2017, 15),
             fontsize=10, fontweight='bold', color='white',
             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='white', lw=1.5))
ax3.annotate(f'Vietnam: {vietnam_share[0]:.1f}% → {vietnam_share[-1]:.1f}%', 
             xy=(supply_x[-1], china_share[-1] + vietnam_share[-1]/2 + 1), 
             xytext=(2023, china_share[-1] + 8),
             fontsize=10, fontweight='bold', color='#375623',
             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#375623', lw=1.5))
ax3.annotate(f'India: {india_share[0]:.1f}% → {india_share[-1]:.1f}%', 
             xy=(supply_x[-1], china_share[-1] + vietnam_share[-1] + india_share[-1]/2 + 0.5), 
             xytext=(2022.5, china_share[-1] + vietnam_share[-1] + india_share[-1] + 5),
             fontsize=10, fontweight='bold', color='#7f3e18',
             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#7f3e18', lw=1.5))

ax3.set_ylabel('Share of Total US Goods Imports (%)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_xlabel('Year', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_xlim(2016, 2024.5)
ax3.set_ylim(0, 100)
ax3.legend(loc='upper right', fontsize=10, framealpha=0.9)
ax3.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linestyle='-', linewidth=0.5, axis='y')
ax3.tick_params(axis='both', labelsize=10)

# Add x-ticks for all years
ax3.set_xticks(range(2016, 2025))
ax3.set_xticklabels([str(y) for y in range(2016, 2025)])

# ===================== SHARED EVENT MARKERS =====================
# Add vertical lines for ALL major policy events across all panels
category_colors = {
    'investigation': '#ff6b6b',
    'tariff': '#ee5a5a',
    'deal': '#7030a0',
    'review': '#4a90e2'
}

event_lines = []
event_labels_legend = []
for e in policy_events:
    date = e['date']
    year = int(date.split('-')[0])
    month = int(date.split('-')[1])
    x_pos = year + (month - 1) / 12
    color = category_colors.get(e['category'], '#888888')
    
    for ax in axes:
        ax.axvline(x=x_pos, color=color, linestyle='-', linewidth=0.8, alpha=0.35, zorder=1)

# Add a compact legend for event categories at bottom
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
legend_elements = [
    Line2D([0], [0], color=category_colors['investigation'], lw=2, label='Investigation'),
    Line2D([0], [0], color=category_colors['tariff'], lw=2, label='Tariff Action'),
    Line2D([0], [0], color=category_colors['deal'], lw=2, label='Trade Deal'),
    Line2D([0], [0], color=category_colors['review'], lw=2, label='Policy Review'),
]
fig.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='lower center', ncol=4, fontsize=10, 
           framealpha=0.9, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.01), title='Policy Event Categories',
           title_fontsize=11)

# ===================== STYLING =====================
# Set background
fig.patch.set_facecolor('white')
for ax in axes:
    ax.set_facecolor('#fafafa')
    for spine in ax.spines.values():
        spine.set_linewidth(0.8)
        spine.set_color('#555555')

# Add panel labels
ax1.text(-0.08, 1.02, 'A', transform=ax1.transAxes, fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', 
         va='bottom', ha='right')
ax2.text(-0.08, 1.02, 'B', transform=ax2.transAxes, fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', 
         va='bottom', ha='right')
ax3.text(-0.08, 1.02, 'C', transform=ax3.transAxes, fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', 
         va='bottom', ha='right')

# Add subtitle panels
ax1.text(0.02, 0.95, 'Tariff Escalation Timeline', transform=ax1.transAxes, 
         fontsize=11, fontweight='bold', va='top', ha='left', color='#333333')
ax2.text(0.02, 0.95, 'Bilateral Trade Volume', transform=ax2.transAxes, 
         fontsize=11, fontweight='bold', va='top', ha='left', color='#333333')
ax3.text(0.02, 0.95, 'Supply Chain Diversion (US Import Shares)', transform=ax3.transAxes, 
         fontsize=11, fontweight='bold', va='top', ha='left', color='#333333')

# Tight layout with space for bottom legend
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.97])

# Save
plt.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=200, bbox_inches='tight', 
            facecolor='white', edgecolor='none')
print("Chart saved successfully to /app/output/result.png")

The chart has been successfully generated and saved to `/app/output/result.png`. 

It's a publication-ready, multi-panel visualization (3089×3318 px PNG) that covers all five insight goals from the task:

- **Panel A** — Tariff escalation timeline with stepwise rate patterns and annotated policy milestones (Section 301, List 1–4 tariffs, Biden-era increases)
- **Panel B** — Bilateral trade volume trajectory showing the 2019–2020 dip during peak tariffs and the subsequent partial recovery
- **Panel C** — Supply-chain diversion as a stacked-area chart highlighting China's declining US import share (21.4% → 12.8%) against the concurrent rise of Vietnam (2.1% → 4.9%) and India (2.1% → 3.4%)

All data is traceable to `source_data.json`, the color scheme is editorial/professional, and labels, legends, and units are included throughout.
